why: The tables of three room kinds the owner asked for after pass 3 (docs/mechanics/DUNGEON_PASS2.md 'Next phase'): bank_vault (a code on signs in other rooms opens a vault), wishing_well (throw an item in, a gamble on its value) and bait_room (leave a bait; the NEXT run spawns a Pokemon lured by it). Read by tools/dungeon_extras.py. Control blocks come from data/dungeon_puzzles.json (the same console, button, lamp and plinth); GREED's prices from data/dungeon_greed.json. Nothing here is an authored dungeon's content: a dungeon's record names the rooms.

bank_vault.budget_why: A bank vault's chests are weighed like a vault's (GREED chest_cp) and held to the same limit KIT3 set (data/dungeon_greed.json vault_budget): all the chests together at most dollar_factor x the gathering tier open at the band's lowest badge count x the shortest dungeon's required hours. The kit's own vault does not enforce it yet (its authors have not rebalanced); a new kind starts inside it.

messages.hint: A code lock. The digits are written elsewhere.

wishing_well.ev_why: The well pays a share of the thrown item's GREED value (cp), rounded DOWN into a currency item, so the pay is at most share x value whatever is thrown: no item is worth more in the well than at the bank. The expected share of a band's table (sum of weight x share) is held at or under ev_cap, so throwing the reward back in loses more each time, and a gambler still has a 'more' tail (share 200 to 500) and a 'nothing' mass.
wishing_well.gaming_why: What cannot be gamed, and how. (1) Worthless items: the well prices a thrown item from GREED's table and refuses anything unpriced, a placeholder price (source 'unpriced': rare candy, exp candies, bamboo blocks) or under min_cp; it throws the item back out of the well. (2) Re-throwing the reward: at most `throws` per run; the expected share is under ev_cap so it loses on average; and GREED charges only a gain (pay minus thrown value, only when above 0), a ratchet that never refunds a loss, so a chain of throws is charged at least the net gain it makes. (3) Carried-in wealth: a gain is charged, not free; the clock only gets faster. (4) Stacks: the value is cp x count, so a stack of cheap items is the sum, and the pay is capped at max_count of the currency item.
wishing_well.shares_why: [weight, share in percent of the thrown value]. Weights sum to 100 (the well rolls random value 1..100). Share 0 is 'nothing'; 50 and 100 are the middling returns; 200, 300 and 500 are the 'more' (a chance of a better return than the gift).
wishing_well.ladders_why: [item, plural name] in rising GREED price (the generator reads each price from data/dungeon_greed.json). The pay is made in the dearest item whose price the pay reaches: a small win is iron, a big one a better thing ('more or better'). The first item must be cheap enough that the smallest real pay (min_cp x the smallest non-zero share) buys one.

messages.hint: Throw something of worth into the well.
messages.cheap: The well wants something of worth.

bait_room.why: BAIT is any item named here; Cobblemon's own bait (the fishing effects in data/cobblemon/spawn_bait_effects of the 1.8.0 jar) is a rod mechanic and is NOT used: only the item ids are. The species is ours: what the lure brings, by bait and band. The Pokemon is spawned at the band's LOWER cap (the prize's reasoning, tools/dungeon_prize.py: the level cap's ball refusal never fires), wandering and catchable, in a living room of the run, and weighs on the clock as an ambient catch.

messages.hint: Leave a bait on the altar.
messages.laid: The bait is laid. Something will follow it.
messages.full: The altar already holds a bait.
